| Servings = 20 hallacas

}}
__NOTOC__
{{recipe}} | [[Cookbook:Cuisine of Venezuela|Cuisine of Venezuela]]

'''Hallaca''' (pronounced ah-YA-kah) is the main Venezuelan Christmas dinner dish. It was created by the slaves during the colony times, who put the left-overs of their masters' Christmas festivities in a bit of cornmeal dough, wrapped this with banana leaves and cooked to mix the flavors. As many things in Venezuela, the hallaca has the influence of three cultures: the white one (European ingredients like raisins, nuts and olives), the native one (the corn meal colored with annatto seeds), and the black one (banana leaves used to cook the food). The original hallaca is made with meat (pork, poultry, beef, lard, crisp pork rind, etc) and boiled eggs.  

Hallaca requires hours of preparation, but it is usually prepared by the whole family—its preparation is a celebration by itself, where music and drinks make up the festive atmosphere. Mothers nagging children as they steal bits of fillings from the table, and the guys complaining of being relegated to the leaf cleaning and last minute shopping are typical during the hallaca making party. 

Make sure you have enough friends and family to help you with the procedure below, and that they include people who know how to fold them once filled, wrap them and tie them properly. 

==Ingredients==

=== Dough ===

* [[Cookbook:Olive Oil|Olive oil]]
* 1 [[Cookbook:Teaspoon|tsp]] [[Cookbook:Annatto|annatto seeds]] (also called "achiote" or "onoto")
* 1 tsp [[Cookbook:Cumin|cumin seeds]]
* 1 tsp [[Cookbook:Pepper|black peppercorns]]
* 1 tsp [[Cookbook:Coriander|coriander seeds]]
* 4 [[Cookbook:Onion|white onions]], [[Cookbook:Slicing|sliced]]
* 1 vegetable [[Cookbook:Bouillon Cube|stock cube]]
* 1 mushroom stock cube
* 1 tsp [[Cookbook:Marmite|marmite]] 
* 2 [[Cookbook:Leek|leeks]], green and white parts cut in 1-[[Cookbook:Inch|inch]] chunks
* 1 large bunch of fresh [[Cookbook:Spices and herbs|herbs]] ([[Cookbook:Cilantro|coriander leaf]], [[Cookbook:Thyme|thyme]], [[Cookbook:Parsley|parsley]], [[Cookbook:Celery|celery]])
* 2 packets of [[Cookbook:Green Onion|spring onions]], [[Cookbook:Chopping|chopped]]
* 1 head of [[Cookbook:Garlic|garlic]], halved
* 1 jar of green [[Cookbook:Olive|olives]] 
* 1 jar of [[Cookbook:Caper|capers]] 
* 1 [[Cookbook:Kilogram|kg]] instant [[Cookbook:Polenta|polenta meal]] (coarse corn meal)
* 500 [[Cookbook:Gram|g]] cooked and mashed [[Cookbook:Potato|new potatoes]] 

=== Fillings ===
[[Image:Ingredientes fundamentales de una hallaca.JPG|right|thumb|Just some of the ingredients for Hallaca]]

* Olive oil
* 2 red [[Cookbook:Bell Pepper|bell peppers]]
* 2 [[Cookbook:Carrot|carrots]], shredded
* 6 [[Cookbook:Brussels Sprout|Brussels sprouts]], shredded
* 1 handful of [[Cookbook:Green Bean|green beans]], [[Cookbook:Chopping|chopped]]
* 100 g mixed vine fruit
* Cooking [[Cookbook:Wine|wine]]
* 20 [[Cookbook:Prune|prunes]]
* 1 can of [[Cookbook:Chickpea|chickpeas]]
* 1 jar of mixed pickles in [[Cookbook:Mustard|mustard]] sauce
* 50 g [[Cookbook:Almond|almonds]]
* 1 can of mock duck or 1 packet of marinated [[Cookbook:Tofu|tofu]] pieces
* 1 can of [[Cookbook:Artichoke|artichoke hearts]]
* 1 can of [[Cookbook:Asparagus|asparagus]]

=== Sauce ===

* Olive oil
* 2 red onions, sliced
* 1 leek, white part chopped
* 1 packet of ''mi-cuit'' (half dried) [[Cookbook:Tomato|tomatoes]] or 1 tube of [[Cookbook:Tomato Paste|tomato paste]]
* 2 red bell peppers
* 2 green bell peppers
* [[Cookbook:Soy Sauce|Soy sauce]]
* [[Cookbook:Chili Paste|Chili sauce]]
* Ground cumin
* Cooking wine (optional)
* Wheat [[Cookbook:Flour|flour]] or [[Cookbook:Cornstarch|cornstarch]]

== Special equipment ==

* 1 roll of kitchen [[Cookbook:Twine|string]]
* 1 kg [[Cookbook:Banana|banana leaves]]

==Procedure==
===Leaves===
# With a damp cloth, wipe the banana leaves.
# Heat the banana leaves over a flame (gas cooker, camping fire, etc). The leaves should turn softer and darker, with a distinctive smoky smell.
# Cut the hard rim without shredding the leaves. Cut in 30 cm segments along the transversal veins

===Dough===
# In a small pan, warm 5 tsp olive oil with the annatto seeds for 20 minutes over very low heat. The oil should turn red. [[Cookbook:Straining|Strain]] to remove the seeds.
# In the meantime, [[Cookbook:Frying|fry]] the cumin, black pepper, and coriander seeds in 2–3 tsp olive oil in a deep pan. 
# Add the white onion, 5 cups of boiling water, stock cubes, Marmite, chunked leeks, fresh herbs, three-quarters of the chopped spring onions, and garlic head.
# [[Cookbook:Simmering|Simmer]] this broth for 15 minutes. 
# Put the contents of the pot in a [[Cookbook:Food Processor|food processor]] and liquidise it. Strain the mixture very well, keeping the liquid and discarding the solids. 
# Put the broth in a large bowl, then add the annatto oil along with the liquid from the olive and the caper jars.
# Add the polenta meal, 1 cup at a time, stirring very well. The consistency should be that of a smooth [[Cookbook:Dough|dough]].
# Mix the mashed potatoes with the polenta dough.
# Test the consistency of the dough: Wrap 1 tsp dough with a small segment of banana leaf. Wrap it in aluminum foil and boil it in water for 15 minutes. If the cooked dough maintain the shape of the banana leaf "package", the dough is ready. If it crumbles or comes out half dissolved in water, then add more polenta meal. If it comes out rock hard, then add more water to the dough. Adjust the salt content as well.

===Fillings===
# Rub olive oil on 2 red bell peppers and [[Cookbook:Grilling|grill]] them all over to char the skin.
# Remove the skin and seeds and cut in 1 cm-wide strips. Set aside in a small bowl.
# Vegetables: Combine the carrot, Brussels sprout, and green beans. Set aside in a small bowl.
# Soak the vine fruit in cooking wine or replacement. Set aside in a small bowl.
# Soak prunes in cooking wine or replacement. Set aside in a small bowl.
# Drain chickpeas and set aside in a small bowl.
# Set pickles aside in a small bowl.
# Blanch and toast the almonds, and set aside in a small bowl.
# Drain and chop the mock duck into 1 cm cubes and set aside in a small bowl.
# Put the olives in a small bowl.
# Put the capers in a small bowl.
# Drain the artichoke hearts, cut in quarters and set aside in a small bowl.
# Drain the asparagus and put it on a plate.

===Sauce===
# Quickly stir-fry the red onion, chopped leek, and the remaining chopped spring onions.
# Using a food processor, liquidise the tomatoes, and peppers. Add to the cooking onions and leek, and stir for a minute.
# Add soy sauce, chili sauce, and ground cumin to season. Add some cooking wine if you want. Let it [[Cookbook:Simmering|simmer]] for another minute.
# Add some flour to thicken. Set the sauce aside in a bowl.

===Assembly===
[[Image:Ingredientes fundamentales de la Hallaca.JPG|right|thumb|Wrapping the hallaca]]
# Cut a 35 cm-long piece of aluminum foil and put it over the table. Cover with a banana leaf, with the transversal veins along the horizontal axis.
# Rub oil on the surface of the banana leaf. Put a bit more than half a ladle of dough in the centre of the leaf. Spread with a spoon to make a 14 cm-diameter circle.
# Put 1 tsp sauce in the middle. Put 1½ tsp shredded vegetables over the sauce. Add 2 olives and 2 capers, one on each corner of the dough. Keep placing the rest of the fillings as in a collage: 1 tsp vine fruit, 1 prune, 2 tsp pickles, 1 tsp chickpeas, 3 cubes of mock duck, 1 asparagus, 2 strips of grilled pepper, and some leaves of parsley.
# Wrap the filling with the banana leaf (not against the veins). Fold the foil to seal the ends of the banana leaf packet. Then, fold the foil to wrap the whole packet. Tie it with kitchen string. Repeat for the rest of the dough.
# [[Cookbook:Boiling|Boil]] the hallacas in a covered pot of water for 20–30 minutes. You may have to do this in batches unless you have a huge cauldron.
# Drain the hallacas and let them cool for 10 hours. Store them in the fridge or freezer if desired.
# Reheat the hallacas in boiling water, [[Cookbook:Simmering|simmering]] for 10 minutes before eat them. Enjoy your meal!

== Notes, tips, and variations ==

* Hallaca tastes better once it has cooled.
* The banana leaves are not intended to be eaten; they are just for cooking!
* You can replace the carrots, brussels sprouts, and green beans with a similar combination of vegetables.
* For overseas expatriates and daring cooks, you can replace the banana leaves with 20x30cm piece of strong [[Cookbook:Aluminium Foil|aluminium foil]].
* For a more old-fashioned meat filling, you can add a whole leg of [[Cookbook:Pork|pork]] or 2–3 roasting [[Cookbook:Chicken|hens]].
